definition: After being captured, Tang Sanzang sends distress signals through 10 methods — each signal's effectiveness determines whether he survives until rescue arrives; this is the 'victim survival science' of monster sociology.

cases: Weeping all day while imprisoned by Yellow Robe Demon in Precious Elephant Kingdom
Crying while hung from a beam at Pansi Cave
signal_methods.mechanism: pure emotional release · no information conveyed · the other party receives no signal

cases: Chanting the Heart Sutra in the cave after being captured by Golden Horn and Silver Horn at Pingding Mountain
Silently invoking Guanyin while pressured by the Rat Demon at the Bottomless Cave
signal_methods.mechanism: seeking psychological refuge through religious ritual · occasional flashes of inspiration
signal_methods.verdict: a psychological defense mechanism · limited real-world effect

cases: The king of Wuji sends a dream to Tang Sanzang seeking help
Sending a dream to the disciples while imprisoned by the Green Ox Demon
signal_methods.mechanism: conveying information through dreams · the receiver must have spiritual sensitivity
signal_methods.verdict: effective for ghosts / victims · Tang Sanzang rarely initiates dream visits

cases: Princess Baihuaxiu of Precious Elephant Kingdom sends a blood-letter to Tang Sanzang
The Queen of the Womanland sends a travel permit
signal_methods.mechanism: conveying distress through a token · requires outside assistance
signal_methods.verdict: moderately effective · depends on whether the token arrives

cases: Villagers of Chen Village tip off in the Goldfish Demon incident
The old soft-shelled turtle of the Tongtian River voluntarily ferries them across
Princess Iron Fan resents Wukong for her son's capture but does not kill Tang Sanzang
signal_methods.mechanism: figures inside or on the margins of a demon's lair pass word out of sympathy
signal_methods.verdict: unstable probability · depends on the demon's temperament

cases: Wukong sees through White Bone Demon's transformation at a glance
The Six-eared Macaque is hard to distinguish but is ultimately exposed
Spider Demon's transformation is seen through by Wukong
signal_methods.mechanism: the Fiery Eyes can see through transformations · proactively identifying threats
signal_methods.verdict: the most reliable passive signal · but requires Wukong to be present

cases: In the Red Boy incident, Bajie goes to the South Sea to summon Guanyin
In the Green Ox Demon incident, Bajie is captured in the first battle · later coordinates help
At Lion-Camel Ridge, Bajie goes to the South Sea to summon Guanyin
signal_methods.mechanism: though lazy, Bajie's ability to seek help is not weak · often serving as a secondary rescue channel

cases: In the Tongtian River incident, Sandy guards the luggage
After many captures, Sandy passively waits for Wukong to handle it
signal_methods.mechanism: Sandy's passive personality · waiting for rescue rather than actively seeking help
signal_methods.verdict: lowest signal-transmission efficiency · but steadily holds his post

cases: In the Yellow Robe Demon incident at Precious Elephant Kingdom, the White Dragon Horse transforms into a palace maid to assassinate
In the Yellow Robe Demon incident, the White Dragon Horse urges Bajie to find Wukong
signal_methods.mechanism: though silent, the White Dragon Horse transforms into human form at key moments to relay messages or act
signal_methods.verdict: low frequency but high efficiency · acts at critical moments

cases: The Jade Emperor sends Taibai Jinxing to forewarn of trouble ahead
Tathāgata arranges things in advance (e.g. Golden Horn and Silver Horn descending as a trial)
Guanyin repeatedly hints at upcoming trials
signal_methods.mechanism: the Heavenly Court / Spirit Mountain forewarns · but often in cryptic terms that are hard to interpret
signal_methods.verdict: vague information · only verifiable after the fact

survival_insights: Tang Sanzang's own ability to call for help is extremely weak · crying + chanting have only 5–10% survival · he must rely on outside rescue
Wukong's Fiery Eyes are the most reliable 'passive signal' · but only if Wukong is present and not deceived
though silent, the White Dragon Horse is a key turning point in the Yellow Robe Demon incident · revealing 'the high value of low-key roles'
Sandy's 'waiting mode' is the least efficient · reflecting his passive personality
Heavenly Court warnings exist but are vague · revealing the court's 'limited intervention' principle
among the 10 signals, active signals average 70% survival and passive signals 15% · a striking gap
